item.strong: SRS v1 · SRS Overview: Digital KYC Onboarding for Banking Clients

srs.title: SRS Overview: Digital KYC Onboarding for Banking Clients
srs.summary: The system facilitates digital Know Your Customer (KYC) onboarding for banking entities, supporting Aadhaar-based e-KYC, offline Aadhaar verification, and fallback mechanisms. The solution must primarily utilize Aadhaar e-KYC authentication, with mandatory fallback to offline verification if e-KYC (
assumptions: The bank operates under regulations that allow any teller or call center staff to perform physical verification for offline cases, excluding the requirement for a designated 'authorized official' unless specific high-risk scenarios apply.
The system relies on external integrations with the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) for Aadhaar authentication and the Central KYC Registry (CKYCR) for data retrieval.
Mobile number mismatches between the customer's Aadhaar and the bank's records will trigger an error during the authentication phase, requiring customer-side resolution before the bank can proceed.
stakeholders: Bank Staff (Tellers, Call Center agents for offline/physical verification)
Bank Authorized Officials (for specific CDD cases involving certified OVD copies or when physical verification is mandatory per context)

findings.text: Clarification required on the escalation logic for e-KYC failure. The user states to 'Always fallback to offline,' but regulations distinguish between simple e-KYC failure (use certified OVD copy or O

The distinction between 'Any staff' and 'Authorized officials' requires definition. Regulation E3 implies offline verification for disabled/elderly customers must be done by an 'official,' whereas the
Video KYC requirements are partially defined in the brief and Answer A, but lack procedural depth. Evidence E2 mandates checks for liveness, absence of prompting, and consideration of customer status

risks.title: Compliance Risk (Verification Authority)
risks.text: Using generic staff for all offline verifications may violate specific regulatory clauses (E3) requiring an 'official' of the RE for certain document verifications, leading to audit failures.

risks.title: Operational Risk (Fallback Complexity)
risks.text: Implementing a blanket 'always fallback to offline' strategy ignores the hierarchy of proofs suggested in E5 (e-KYC > Offline Aadhaar > Certified OVD), potentially leading to inefficient user journeys

risks.title: Technical Risk (Mobile Number Validation)
risks.text: The system must enforce strict mobile number matching (E4); failure to validate this will cause immediate authentication rejection, which may frustrate customers with valid but mismatched mobile data.

openIssues: Confirm the exact regulatory threshold or customer class where 'authorized official' overrides 'any staff' for offline verification.
Define the precise workflow hierarchy: Does the system attempt e-KYC -> Offline -> Certified OVD in sequence, or does it allow user selection?
Specify the criteria for 'injury, illness, infirmity' to trigger the offline verification fallback for subsidies/benefits versus general account opening.

requirements.statement: The system shall default to Offline Aadhaar verification or certified OVD submission if e-KYC authentication fails for any customer.
requirements.acceptance: 100% of e-KYC failures must trigger a fallback workflow to Offline Aadhaar or Certified OVD capture within 24 hours of failure notification.

requirements.statement: Authentication requests for Aadhaar number shall be routed exclusively to the e-KYC facility provided by the UIDAI.
requirements.acceptance: 100% of Aadhaar authentication requests must be processed via the external UIDAI API; no internal mock authentication shall be used.

requirements.statement: Any staff member (teller or call center) must be permitted to initiate the physical verification for offline cases and e-KYC rejections, provided they possess a valid staff ID.
requirements.acceptance: The system shall authenticate and authorize any verified staff member for the verification workflow, regardless of role hierarchy, without requiring a specific 'Officer' title.

requirements.statement: For video KYC interactions, the system shall dynamically vary liveness detection prompts (e.g., head turns, reading text) throughout the session to ensure real-time presence.
requirements.acceptance: The session must reject the customer immediately if liveness checks are static, pre-recorded, or if the customer fails three consecutive liveness prompts.

requirements.statement: The system shall automatically reject the account opening workflow if the customer exhibits prompting (e.g., reading instructions) at the end of the video interaction.
requirements.acceptance: 100% of video sessions containing detected prompting at the conclusion shall result in a hard system rejection of the KYC status.

requirements.statement: The system shall verify the digital signature of OVDs against the Information Technology Act, 2000 provisions and capture a live photograph of the customer for OVDs that lack digital signatures.
requirements.acceptance: 100% of uploaded OVDs without valid digital signatures must trigger a mandatory live photo capture step before KYC approval; invalid signatures result in automatic rejection.

requirements.statement: The system shall record audio-video and capture a photograph of the customer present for identification during the entire physical verification process.
requirements.acceptance: Every offline verification session must generate a complete media file (audio + video + photo) that is successfully stored in the secure repository; missing media results in case c

requirements.statement: The system shall redact or blackout the Aadhaar number in all stored logs, generated reports, and user-facing interfaces in accordance with privacy regulations.
requirements.acceptance: 100% of stored records containing Aadhaar numbers must show the number masked (e.g., XXXXXXXX-1234) except in specific authorized regulatory reports where de-masking requires a PIN

requirements.statement: The system shall retrieve KYC records online from the Central KYC Registry (CKYCR) only when an explicit customer consent is provided and a valid KYC Identifier is supplied.
requirements.acceptance: KYC data retrieval from the CKYCR gateway must return a 'Consent Pending' or 'Access Denied' error if no explicit consent flag is present in the request payload.

requirements.statement: The system must categorize customers based on risk levels (Low, Medium, High) and restrict data retention/deletion schedules according to the derived risk category and banking regulations.
requirements.acceptance: Risk categorization must be automated based on input data (e.g., nationality, address type) and the system must enforce retention policies (e.g., High Risk = 6 years) without user
